piece_type: HCP branded website webpages ("Efficacy and 2-year patient outcomes" and "Real VYEPTI experience")
regs_in_letter: FD&C Act misbranding (false or misleading); no CFR section cited in letter text

cases.cat: Misleading presentation of study data (post hoc / exploratory)
cases.heading: (none; body text)
cases.claim: “During a 6-month chronic migraine pivotal study, 40% of patients treated with VYEPTI 300 mg were 100% migraine free for a month or more vs 22% with placebo” | “Give your patients the chance for 100% migraine freedom for a month or more” | “During the same period, 35% of patients treated with VYPETI 100 mg were 100% migraine free for a month or more vs 22% with placebo.”
cases.context: Presented in conjunction with a prominent graphic of a woman standing in front of a large 100% image; "Post hoc analysis" appears only as a less prominent footnote, which FDA says does not mitigate the impression.
cases.rationale: Claims rest on a post hoc analysis of PROMISE-1/2 with no prespecified type 1 error control, so findings are exploratory; conclusory '100% migraine freedom' claims are unsupported and imply patients will be migraine-free.
cases.check: Does the piece present results from post hoc / non-prespecified analyses as conclusive efficacy, with the post hoc caveat relegated to a footnote?

cases.heading: (none; body text)
cases.claim: “Reduce the impact of migraine for your patients” | “Patients on VYEPTI 300 mg experienced SUSTAINED REDUCTION in average headache pain severity over 2 years” | “>70% of patients on VYEPTI 300 mg reported their migraine symptoms were MUCH IMPROVED or VERY MUCH IMPROVED through 2 years” | “Increase potential for patient productivity and engagement in everyday life” | “>60% of patients on VYEPTI 300 mg reported IMPROVEMENT IN MIGRAINE ASSOCIATED DISABILITY through 2 years” | “Patients saw improvement in disability from first dose through 2 years, which resulted in more engagement at home, work, and in their social life”
cases.context: Claims based on PREVAIL (open-label, single-arm) and a post hoc analysis; accompanied by graphs of MIDAS severity, PGIC, and MIDAS score over weeks 0-104.
cases.rationale: PRO endpoints (HIT-6, MIDAS, PGIC) had no alpha allocation and came from an open-label single-arm trial; instruments have validity/recall-bias limitations, so conclusory PRO/HRQoL claims are unsupported.
cases.check: Are patient-reported outcome, disability, or quality-of-life benefit claims supported by a controlled, alpha-controlled endpoint using a fit-for-purpose instrument?

cases.heading: (none; body text)
cases.claim: “~70% of patients reported increased satisfaction with their ability TO PLAN, BE PRODUCTIVE, AND PARTICIPATE in their daily lives” | “After starting VYEPTI, patients reported >2x THE AMOUNT OF MONTHLY GOOD DAYS” | “Of the 74 patients who stated they experience brain fog, 86% REPORTED IMPROVEMENT IN BRAIN FOG”
cases.context: "Real VYEPTI experience" webpage; presented with attention-grabbing, colorful, bold graphics and charts with large font; based on REVIEW, an observational single-arm study.
cases.rationale: REVIEW had selection bias (required >=2 infusion cycles), no control arm, endpoints lacking validity/standard definitions, and long retrospective recall, so PRO claims are unsupported.
cases.check: Does the piece cite real-world/observational single-arm data to claim patient-reported benefits (satisfaction, 'good days', 'brain fog') as if causally attributable to the drug?
